// @path: src/lib/ops/reads.ts
// A string literal whose LAST word is `import`. Not an import statement, and it
// must not be read as one.
//
// The regression this pins, found on 2026-08-24: the bare-import pattern was
// `\bimport\s*["']`, and `\s*` matches zero characters, so the `import` at the
// end of "gias:import" matched with that string's CLOSING quote taken as an
// opening one. The scanner then captured everything up to the next quote in the
// file and refused the file for importing a package called
//     " },\n    orderBy: [{ startedAt: "
//
// It is the same fault as F52 in a different scanner: a closing quote mistaken
// for an opening one. Two of them in one repository is a pattern rather than a
// coincidence, which is why this is pinned rather than worked around.
//
// It WAS worked around first: the job key was renamed to "register:refresh" so
// the literal no longer ended in the word. That is a product constant bent to
// suit a tool bug, and the tool bug is fixed now, but the name is fine and
// should stay. This fixture keeps the scanner honest whatever the key is called.
import { db } from "@/lib/db";

export async function lastRunOfEachJob() {
  const jobs = ["register:refresh", "mail:suppression-sync", "gias:import"];
  return db.jobRun.findMany({
    where: { job: { in: jobs } },
    orderBy: [{ startedAt: "desc" }],
    select: { job: true, startedAt: true, outcome: true, itemsAffected: true },
  });
}
